decisions.quote: Similarly, using other thresholds generally leads to differing results for the WHN and MHN treatments especially, but importantly for the findings of the paper, the effect of the WCommHN treatment is always consistent at (at least) the 5% significance level on both rice and meat/fish expenditure, except in the case where no trimming is used. Similarly, its effect is consistently greater than that of the other two treatments on meat/fish expenditure, and thus the main conclusion of the paper is robust to different trimming methods even though the results for the other treatments vary.
decisions.location: Section 3.5.3, pp. 7-8, lines 295-302 (also Abstract, p. 1, lines 24-27; Section 4, p. 8, lines 320-332; Section 11, p. 10, lines 391-393)
decisions.reason: The codebook instructs coders to settle each axis over the re-analyses together rather than picking one, and explicitly states regarding robustness challenges: 'where the authors state explicitly how they read the variation, trust their judgement.' Although completely removing outlier trimming in Table 4 causes the standalone level coefficient on meat/fish expenditure to become marginally insignificant while keeping the treatment-arm comparisons (WCommHN vs. WHN and MHN) and animal-sourced food intake ASTE significant, all five alternative trimming and winsorizing thresholds (1%, 5%, 10%) preserve the effect, and the authors explicitly judge in Section 3.5.3 that 'the main conclusion of the paper is robust to different trimming methods.' They likewise conclude in the Abstract that 'the results are robust' and in Section 11 that the original results 'withstood our robustness checks performed above.'
